Prealgebra · Lesson 10.6

Mean, Median, and Mode

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Probability gave one number for how likely something is. A list of numbers can be summarized the same way, with one number that stands for the whole list. There are three ways to name the center of a data set, and each answers a different question. The mean is the average, the median is the middle value, and the mode is the value that appears most often.

Problem
Five aquarium tanks along a wall hold 1212, 77, 1515, 99, and 1212 guppies. A keeper scoops guppies from tank to tank until every tank holds the same number, with none added and none removed overall. How many guppies end up in each tank? Give the number.
Show a hint
  • Since no guppies are added or removed, the total across all five tanks stays fixed no matter how they get shuffled around. Start by adding up how many guppies there are altogether.
  • Every tank must end with the same count, so take that total and split it evenly among the 55 tanks. That single equal share is the number each tank ends up holding.
Show the full solution
Moving guppies around does not change the total, so add the five tanks, 12+7+15+9+12=5512+7+15+9+12=55, then split that evenly among the 55 tanks, 555=11.555​=11​. That equal share is the mean, the number you get when you level every value out.
Problem
A kite flyer records how many minutes her kite stayed up on four windy afternoons: 1818, 2525, 2222, and 3030 minutes. What is the mean number of minutes the kite stayed up per afternoon? Give your answer as a decimal.
Show a hint
  • The mean is the total of all the values divided by how many values there are, so first add the four times 18+25+22+3018+25+22+30.
  • The sum is 9595, and there are 44 afternoons, so divide 9595 by 44 and notice the answer does not have to match any single afternoon.
Show the full solution
Add the four recorded times, 18+25+22+30=9518+25+22+30=95, then divide by the 44 afternoons, mean=954=23.75.mean=495​=23.75​. The mean is a balancing point for the whole set, so it can land between the values instead of on one of them.
Problem
A bakery records how many loaves it sells each day from Monday through Friday. On four of the days it sold 4040, 5252, 3838, and 6161 loaves, and the five-day average came out to exactly 4949 loaves. How many loaves were sold on the fifth day? Give the number.
Show a hint
  • The mean is the total divided by the number of days, so if the average of five days is 4949, the five daily counts must add up to 49×549×5. Work out that total first.
  • You know four of the five values, so subtract their sum from the full total. Whatever is left over is the number of loaves sold on the missing day.
Show the full solution
The average of the five days is the total divided by 55, so the five days add to 49×5=24549×5=245. The four known days give 40+52+38+61=19140+52+38+61=191, so the missing day is 245−191=54.245−191=54​. A mean and a count together always hand you the total, which is what makes a missing value findable.
Problem
A coding club has 1212 beginners who averaged 3030 points on a puzzle, and 88 advanced members who averaged 5555 points. What is the average score of all 2020 members together? It is tempting to just average 3030 and 5555, but that ignores how many people are in each group, so think about the total points first. Give the number.
Show a hint
  • The mean of a group is total points divided by number of people, so you can run that backward. A group's total is its mean times its size, which gives 12×3012×30 points for the beginners and 8×558×55 points for the advanced members.
  • Add both totals to get the points scored by all 2020 members, then divide that sum by 2020. Averaging 3030 and 5555 to get 42.542.5 would be wrong here because the two groups are not the same size, and the larger beginner group pulls the true average down.
Show the full solution
Rebuild the totals. The beginners scored 12×30=36012×30=360 points and the advanced members scored 8×55=4408×55=440 points, so all 2020 together scored 800800 points and the average is 12×30+8×5520=80020=40.2012×30+8×55​=20800​=40​. Averaging 3030 and 5555 would give 42.542.5, but the groups are different sizes, and the larger beginner group pulls the combined average down toward its own score.
Key idea
The mean. The mean, or average, is the total of the values divided by how many values there are. mean=sum of the valueshow many values.mean=how many valuessum of the values​. It is the amount each value would have if the total were shared out evenly, and it need not equal any actual value. The formula also works in reverse, sum=mean×countsum=mean×count, so the mean and the count together recover a missing value. To merge two groups, you cannot average the two averages unless the groups are the same size. Rebuild each total, add them, and divide by the total count. The combined mean is closer to the average of the bigger group.
Problem
Seven kids skip stones across a pond and count the skips: 4,9,6,3,8,7,114,9,6,3,8,7,11. The median is the middle score once the list is sorted from smallest to largest. What is the median number of skips? Give the number.
Show a hint
  • The list is scrambled, so sort it from smallest to largest before you look for the middle. Sorting gives 3,4,6,7,8,9,113,4,6,7,8,9,11.
  • With 77 values in order, the middle one is the 44th, since three values sit below it and three sit above it.
Show the full solution
Sort the counts from smallest to largest, 3, 4, 6, 7‾, 8, 9, 11.3, 4, 6, 7​, 8, 9, 11. With 77 values the middle one is the 44th, with three below it and three above it, so the median is 77​. Sorting comes first every time, since middle only means something once the list is in order.
Problem
Six friends compare how many books they read over the summer: 5,12,8,3,9,145,12,8,3,9,14. What is the median number of books? Give your answer as a decimal.
Show a hint
  • The median is the middle value once the data is in order, so start by sorting the six counts from smallest to largest.
  • With six values there is no single middle number, so look at the two values sitting in the middle and take their mean.
Show the full solution
Sort the counts, giving 3,5,8,9,12,143,5,8,9,12,14. Six values means no single number sits in the middle, so take the two middle ones, 88 and 99, and average them, 8+92=172=8.5.28+9​=217​=8.5​. With an even count the median is often not one of the numbers in the list.
Key idea
The median. The median is the middle value once the list is written in order, so sort the numbers first, always. With an odd count one value is in the middle, and that value is the median. With an even count two values are in the middle, and the median is their mean, median=lower middle+upper middle2.median=2lower middle+upper middle​. Like the mean, the median need not be one of the numbers in the list.
Problem
A jacket shop records the sizes it sold today: 6,8,8,10,8,12,8,10,6,86,8,8,10,8,12,8,10,6,8. They want to reorder the most of whichever size sells best, so they need the size that appears most often in the list. Which size should they reorder the most of? Give the size.
Show a hint
  • The size they should reorder most is the mode, the value that appears most often, so tally how many times each size shows up in the list.
  • Count carefully. Size 66 appears twice, size 1010 appears twice, and size 1212 appears once, but one size beats them all, and that highest count is the mode.
Show the full solution
Tally the sizes in 6,8,8,10,8,12,8,10,6,86,8,8,10,8,12,8,10,6,8. Size 66 shows up twice, size 1010 twice, size 1212 once, and size 88 five times, so the most frequent size is 8.8​. The mode is the right summary here, since the shop cares about which size sells most, not about an average size.
Problem
A list can have more than one mode. A survey records these numbers: 2,5,2,7,5,9,5,22,5,2,7,5,9,5,2. Both 22 and 55 appear three times, which is more often than any other value. A value counts as a mode when it ties for the most frequent. How many values are modes?
Show a hint
  • Tally how many times each different value shows up. Count the 22s, the 55s, the 77, and the 99 separately.
  • The mode is the value with the highest count, but if two values share that same top count, they are both modes. Look for which values reach the largest tally and count how many there are.
Show the full solution
Count how often each value appears. The value 22 shows up three times, 55 shows up three times, and 77 and 99 show up once each. Two values tie for the top count of three, so both are modes and the number of modes is 2.2​. A tie for most frequent does not cancel out, it just gives the list two modes, which is what "multimodal" means.
Key idea
The mode. The mode is the value that appears most often. The mean depends on the size of the values and the median on their position. The mode depends only on how often each value shows up. It is the right summary for choices and categories, like the shoe size a store should stock or the most common survey answer. A list where every value is different has no mode, and a list where two values tie for most frequent has two modes.
Problem
A five-person startup pays its four employees 4242, 4848, 4545, and 5151 thousand dollars a year, while the founder earns 314314 thousand. By how many thousand dollars does the mean salary exceed the median salary? Give the number (of thousand dollars).
Show a hint
  • The mean is the total of all five salaries divided by 55, so add 42+48+45+51+31442+48+45+51+314 and split the sum evenly across the five people.
  • The median is the middle value once the salaries are lined up in order, so sort them as 42,45,48,51,31442,45,48,51,314 and read off the one in the center, then subtract it from the mean.
Show the full solution
The mean adds all five salaries and divides by 55, mean=42+48+45+51+3145=5005=100.mean=542+48+45+51+314​=5500​=100. Ordering the salaries as 42,45,48,51,31442,45,48,51,314 puts 4848 in the middle, so the median is 4848 and the gap is 100−48=52.100−48=52​. The four ordinary salaries hold the median in place, while the founder's 314314 thousand pulls the mean far above it. That is what a single large value does to an average.
Problem
A gymnast's five routine scores average 9.29.2. She has one routine left, and she wants her average across all six scores to stay exactly 9.29.2. What score must she earn on the sixth routine? Give your answer as a decimal.
Show a hint
  • The mean is the total of all scores divided by how many there are. With five scores averaging 9.29.2, the current total is 5×9.2=465×9.2=46.
  • After the sixth routine you will divide a new total by 66, and you want that to equal 9.29.2. Ask what sixth score keeps the total-over-count balanced, and notice that adding one more copy of the mean itself leaves the mean untouched.
Show the full solution
Five scores averaging 9.29.2 total 5×9.2=465×9.2=46. Call the sixth score xx, so the six-score average is 46+x6=9.2.646+x​=9.2. Multiply both sides by 66 to get 46+x=55.246+x=55.2, then subtract 4646, so she must score 9.29.2​. Adding one more value equal to the current mean leaves the mean exactly where it was, since you are adding an average-sized share to an average-sized pile.
Problem
A staircase has an LED on every step. The steps show 7,11,15,19,7,11,15,19, and so on, going up by 44 each step, with the top step showing 4343. What is the mean of all the numbers shown? Give the number.
Show a hint
  • The numbers are evenly spaced, each one 44 more than the last, so pair them from the outside in. The smallest 77 pairs with the largest 4343, the next 1111 pairs with 3939, and so on, just like pairing the ends when you add 11 up to nn.
  • Every pair adds to the same total, 7+43=507+43=50, so every number sits the same distance above or below the center. That means you never have to add the whole list, since the mean is just the value halfway between the two ends.
Show the full solution
The numbers are evenly spaced, each one 44 above the last, so pair them from the ends inward. 77 pairs with 4343, 1111 with 3939, 1515 with 3535, and every pair sums to 5050. The values balance around a single center, so the mean is the average of the two ends, 7+432=502=25.27+43​=250​=25​. For any evenly spaced list the mean equals the median and equals the average of the first and last term, so you never have to add the whole thing.
Key idea
Which summary to use. The mean uses every value, so a single outlier shifts it away from the other values. The median depends only on position and barely moves, which makes it the fairer typical value for lopsided data like incomes or prices. The mean is also the balance point of the data. The gaps above it and the gaps below it cancel to zero, so adding a value equal to the mean changes nothing. When the values are evenly spaced, the mean equals the median, and both equal the average of the ends. mean=first+last2.mean=2first+last​. When the mean and median disagree by a lot, the data is skewed.
Fun fact
The word "average" traces back through Old French and Italian to the Arabic "awariya", meaning damaged goods. When a storm ruined part of a ship's cargo, the loss was shared out evenly among all the merchants, and that fair split of a total is exactly what a mean does today.
Problem
A gym sets your membership tier by the median of your nine monthly visit counts. Seven months in, your counts are 20,8,16,5,22,12,1620,8,16,5,22,12,16. You have two months left, and you can visit at most 3030 times in a month. What is the highest median you can reach across all nine months? Give the number.
Show a hint
  • With nine values, the median is the 55th number once they are sorted, so the whole question is where that middle slot lands.
  • Each new month can be at most 3030, which is larger than everything you already have, so both new values drop in above your current numbers and none of them can slide into the 55th slot from below.
Show the full solution
Sort the seven known counts, 5, 8, 12, 16, 16, 20, 22.5, 8, 12, 16, 16, 20, 22. With nine values the median is the 55th, and each new month is at most 3030, which is bigger than everything already on the list, so both new counts land at the top. Adding only above the middle leaves the 55th value right where it was, at 16.16​. Pushing the new months higher stretches the top of the list, never the middle, which is exactly why the median resists big values.
Problem
A set of five positive whole numbers has a mean of 1616, a median of 1515, and 1515 is its only mode. What is the greatest value the largest number in the set could be? Give the number.
Show a hint
  • A mean of 1616 across five numbers fixes the total. Multiply to get the sum, 5×16=805×16=80, so however you fill the five slots they must add to 8080.
  • Sort the five numbers. The median is the 3rd value, so the middle slot is 1515. For 1515 to be the only mode it has to appear at least twice, so make the 4th slot 1515 too, and to leave the largest as big as possible make the two smallest slots the tiniest distinct positive integers that do not tie 1515, namely 11 and 22.
Show the full solution
Five numbers averaging 1616 add to 5×16=805×16=80. Sort the set, so the 3rd slot is the median and holds 1515, and 1515 needs a second copy to be a mode, so slot 4 is 1515 too. To leave the top number as large as possible, make the first two slots the smallest positive whole numbers that do not tie 1515 for most frequent, namely 11 and 22. The largest number takes the rest of the total, 80−(1+2+15+15)=47.80−(1+2+15+15)=47​. Checking, {1,2,15,15,47}{1,2,15,15,47} sums to 8080 for a mean of 1616, has middle value 1515, and repeats only 1515.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Find the mean of the four numbers 1414, 99, 2222, and 1515. Give the number.
Show the solution
Add the four numbers, 14+9+22+15=6014+9+22+15=60, then divide by the 44 values, mean=604=15.mean=460​=15​.
Practice
Find the median of the data set 7,2,9,4,67,2,9,4,6. Give the number.
Show the solution
Sort the five values, giving 2,4,6,7,92,4,6,7,9. With five numbers there is a single middle position, the third, with two numbers below it and two above it, so the median is 66​.
Practice
Find the mode of this data set: 3,7,3,9,3,7,53,7,3,9,3,7,5. Give the number.
Show the solution
Tally how often each number appears. The value 33 shows up three times, 77 twice, and 99 and 55 once each, so the value appearing most often is 33​.
Practice
Find the mean of the four numbers 1010, 1313, 1414, and 1010. Give your answer as a decimal.
Show the solution
Add the four numbers, 10+13+14+10=4710+13+14+10=47, then divide by 44, mean=474=11.75.mean=447​=11.75​. A mean does not have to be a whole number even when every value in the list is.
Practice
A weather station takes five daily temperature readings, and their mean is 2020 degrees. Four of the readings are 1515, 2222, 1818, and 2525. What is the fifth reading? Give the number.
Show the solution
Five readings with a mean of 2020 must total 5×20=1005×20=100. The four known readings add to 15+22+18+25=8015+22+18+25=80, so the fifth is 100−80=20.100−80=20​. It lands right on the mean, which is what happens when the values you already have average out to 2020 on their own.
Practice
Find the median of these six numbers: 12,4,8,20,6,1012,4,8,20,6,10. Give the number.
Show the solution
Sort the six numbers, giving 4,6,8,10,12,204,6,8,10,12,20. With an even count no single value sits in the middle, so average the 33rd and 44th, 8+102=9.28+10​=9​.
Practice
On a test, a group of 1010 students averaged 8080 points and a separate group of 1515 students averaged 9090 points. What is the average score of all 2525 students combined? Give the number.
Show the solution
Rebuild each group's total from its average. The 1010 students averaging 8080 scored 10×80=80010×80=800 points, and the 1515 students averaging 9090 scored 15×90=135015×90=1350 points. Divide the combined total by all 2525 students, giving 800+135025=215025=86.25800+1350​=252150​=86​. The result sits closer to 9090 than to 8080 because the larger group pulls the mean toward its own score.
Practice
A data set has the values 88, 1010, 99, 1111, and 6262. The mean of these five numbers is 2020, and the median is 1010. By how much does the mean exceed the median? Give the number.
Show the solution
The mean is 8+10+9+11+625=1005=2058+10+9+11+62​=5100​=20, and sorting the list to 8,9,10,11,628,9,10,11,62 puts 1010 in the middle, so the difference is 20−10=10.20−10=10​. The outlier 6262 drags the mean well above the typical value while leaving the median untouched, which is why the two centers disagree.
Practice
The ten multiples of 33 from 33 up to 3030 are 3,6,9,…,303,6,9,…,30, and they add up to 165165. Remove one number so that the nine numbers left have a mean of 1616. Which number is removed? Give the number.
Show the solution
Nine numbers with a mean of 1616 must add to 9×16=1449×16=144. All ten add to 165165, so the removed number is the gap between those totals, 165−144=21.165−144=21​. And 2121 really is on the list, since it is a multiple of 33 between 33 and 3030.
Practice
Six different positive whole numbers have a mean of 1010, so they add up to 6060. What is the largest that any single one of them can be? Give the number.
Show the solution
A mean of 1010 across six numbers fixes the total at 6×10=606×10=60. To push one value as high as possible, make the other five as small as they can be, and since they must be different positive whole numbers that is 1,2,3,4,51,2,3,4,5, which adds to 1515. The rest goes to the sixth number, 60−15=45.60−15=45​.
Practice
The mean of five numbers is 1212. A sixth number is added, and the mean of all six numbers rises to 1414. What is the sixth number? Give the number.
Show the solution
The first five numbers total 5×12=605×12=60, and all six total 6×14=846×14=84, so the sixth number is 84−60=24.84−60=24​. Turning each mean back into a total is what makes the added value easy to read off.
Practice
A shoe shop sold these sizes over one afternoon: 7,8,8,9,8,10,7,87,8,8,9,8,10,7,8. The owner wants to restock the most common size, since that is what customers buy the most. Which size should the shop restock the most of? Give the size.
Show the solution
Tally the sizes sold. Size 77 appears twice, 99 once, 1010 once, and 88 appears in four of the eight sales, so the mode is 8.8​. The shop should restock size 88, the size customers bought most often.
Practice
Find the average of all the whole numbers from 4141 to 5959, including both ends. Give the number.
Show the solution
The numbers 41,42,43,…,5941,42,43,…,59 are evenly spaced, one apart, so the mean is the average of the two ends, 41+592=1002=50.241+59​=2100​=50​. That saves adding all nineteen numbers, and it works for any evenly spaced list because the values balance around their center.
Practice
A set of five positive whole numbers has a mean of 66, a median of 66, and 88 as its only mode. What is the difference between the largest and smallest values in the set? Give the number.
Show the solution
A mean of 66 across five numbers fixes the total at 5×6=305×6=30, and a median of 66 puts 66 in the middle slot once they are sorted. For 88 to be the only mode it must appear more than any other value, so the two largest slots are both 88, giving 6,8,86,8,8 and a running total of 2222. The two smallest must add to 30−22=830−22=8 while staying different from each other and from 88, and the pair 33 and 55 works, so the set is 3,5,6,8,83,5,6,8,8 and 8−3=5.8−3=5​.
